title: network-onboarding-brief-compact-audit-playbook
content:
Overview

Short-form playbook for customer-managed network onboarding with a focus on a lightweight, usable audit envelope and clear approval gate choreography. This is intended as a pragmatic PRD-ish guide we can use to prototype a first-pass UX + operator runbook that minimizes friction for customers while preserving post-incident forensic value.

Context / why this exists
- We get repeated feedback that full forensic bundles are heavy for initial onboarding and slow down customer acceptance.
- Security teams need immutable evidence for critical VPC changes, but operators want a fast and predictable first-touch flow.
- Existing artifacts in the repo explore detailed attestation/ledger solutions; this doc sketches a compact, staged approach that scales from "first-touch" onboarding to full attestation later.

Problem statement
Customers struggle with three tension points during private VPC onboarding:
1) Friction: requiring large evidentiary uploads and lengthy approvals blocks on-prem/air-gapped deliveries.
2) Cost/complexity: full-forensics retention and retention policies increase storage/ingest costs.
3) Investigability: too-small audit records hinder post-incident reconstruction.

Goal (what success looks like)
- Provide a minimal audit envelope that: (a) captures necessary metadata to reconstruct intent and identity; (b) is tamper-evident; (c) is small (< 50 KB typical) and easy to transmit over constrained channels.
- Design onboarding approval gates that allow a fast operator-approved path ("fast-accept") and an optional elevated-review path for high-risk customers.
- Deliver an operator runbook and sample payload so solutions eng can onboard first customers within 2 weeks of feature availability.

Non-goals
- This doc does not prescribe an enterprise-grade immutable ledger or long-term attestation retention policy — those remain in the full attestation RAID/ledger workstream.
- We are not building a complete SIEM-forwarding stack here. Integration templates will be separate.

Primary users and personas
- Customer operator (first-touch): performs onboarding, provides evidence, expects quick time-to-connect.
- Security reviewer (customer/RW): inspects evidence, can request escalation.
- Redwood Onboarding engineer: reviews minimal evidence and approves host handshake.

Product decisions and rationale (summary)
- Use a two-tier evidence model: Compact Audit Envelope (CAE) for onboarding + Forensic Capsule (FC) for deep incident work.
- CAE intentionally contains canonical metadata, a short human summary, a condensed diff of network changes, and a compact signature block. No packet captures, no long logs.
- CAE must be serializable to a small JSON string (we will compress/base64 when sending across constrained endpoints) and be validated server-side.

Requirements (MUST/HIGH/MED/LOW)
- MUST: CAE includes timestamp, actor identity (OID/email+id), action type (create/update/delete), resource canonical id (VPC id/ASN/subnet ids), short-change summary (2–6 lines), and request-id.
- MUST: CAE includes integrity proof (ECDSA signature or HMAC depending on channel) and a server-side verification path.
- MUST: Approval flow supports operator "fast-accept" with optional post-accept audit queuing.
- HIGH: CAE stores a small pointer to a Forensic Capsule if one exists (s3 path or SFTP manifest) without inlining it.
- MED: We provide a compact UI card in Console with a one-click view and accept/reject that surfaces risk hints.
- LOW: Allow customers to opt-in to automated SIEM forwarding from the CAE.

Approval gate choreography (proposal)
1) Submit CAE — customer operator completes online onboarding form and uploads CAE via signed API.
2) Automatic checks — basic syntactic/semantic validation (id present, timestamp not in future, resource id format).
3) Risk heuristics — evaluate resource types and sensitive flags (eg. public egress, NAT changes). If below threshold, present "Fast-accept" badge.
4) Operator review — Redwood onboarding engineer sees the CAE card (compact summary + trace links) and can Accept / Request More Evidence / Escalate. Accept path marks the VPC as connected.
5) Post-accept work — schedule (optional) full Forensic Capsule collection within N days (configurable) for customers who want immutability.

Operator runbook (draft)
- Step 0: Pre-checks: confirm customer has signed NDA/SLA. Check onboarding ticket linked (JIRA).
- Step 1: Inspect CAE card: scan the 2–6 line summary and change diff. Check actor identity and if signature verifies.
- Step 2: Quick heuristics: are there public CIDR allocations? cross-account peering? If yes, escalate.
- Step 3: If everything looks good, click Accept and optionally tick "Collect FC within 72h".
- Step 4: If suspicious, mark Request More Evidence and send templated evidence request (sample playbook included below).

Sample compact audit envelope (CAE) - human readable example
(we keep this textual and intentionally small — example payload compressed here)

CAE 1-line header: "CAE:v1 | request=PRIV-2024-0732 | actor=riley.chen@redwood.ai"

Short payload (example, single-line break formatting preserved):
- timestamp: 2024-06-12T18:34:12Z
- actor: riley.chen@redwood.ai (OID: u-9b23)
- action: add-route
- resource_ids: vpc-01a23b
- summary: "Add peer route to customer peering; destination 10.12.0.0/16 -> peer-acc-739; intended for model-data egress"
- diff-snippet: "route table rt-9a -> +10.12.0.0/16 via pcx-739"
- signature: "ecdsa:BASE64SIG..."

Notes: The CAE should be under ~50KB in practice. The Console card will render the summary, the diff-snippet, and a short risk flag. Full FC is referenced via pointer if available.

Forensics and replay considerations
- When an incident requires replay, the forensic stack will pull the referenced FC and related telemetry (if flagged). The CAE acts as the breadcrumb trail for quick triage.
- FC contents (outside scope here) include full flow logs, operator chat transcripts, and immutable snapshots.

Metrics / success criteria (first 90 days)
- Mean time to onboard (first connection) for customers using CAE < 48 hours.
- Fraction of onboardings completed via Fast-accept > 60% for low-risk customers.
- Operator time per CAE < 6 minutes (median).
- CAE size median < 20 KB.

UX mock notes and console card (quick)
- Card header: Customer name, VPC id, request id, time, risk badge (green/amber/red)
- Body: 2–3 line summary + diff-snippet + "View full FC" link (if pointer present)
- Actions: Accept | Request More Evidence | Escalate (with reason template)

Security and privacy notes
- CAE signatures: when possible prefer customer ECDSA key signed by their KMS. For constrained channels allow HMAC keyed by pre-shared secret during initial handshake.
- Retention: short-lived CAE (30–90d) unless the customer opts-in to longer retention. FC retention and ledger decisions handled by separate policy doc.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q: What exact schema do we standardize on for the diff-snippet — patch-like vs natural language? (TODO: team decision)
- Q: How to manage key exchange for ECDSA for air-gapped customers? (TODO: SRE/infra consult)
- Action: Samir to prototype CAE payload and small validation lambda. (PRIVNET-213)
- Action: Elena to draft minimal console card mock and copy variants for escalations.

Next steps / short timeline (proposal)
- Week 1: prototype CAE schema + validation lambda (Samir).
- Week 2: minimal Console card + operator runbook draft (Elena + Riley).
- Week 3: internal trial with 2 customers (Priya to coordinate).
- Week 4: iterate on schema based on trial feedback and decide on FC pointer protocol.

Appendix: Quick templated evidence request (used for "Request More Evidence")
- Please provide: 1) short annotated network diagram (png), 2) raw change request (git diff or YAML), 3) operator justification note (1–3 paragraphs), 4) signature block + timestamp.

Notes-to-self (Riley)
- Keep CAE intentionally limited; we can always expand fields later.
- Lean on existing attestation work for the FC pointer standard, but don't require it for first-pass sign-offs.
- Monitor operator time; if > 10 mins we iterate on the card UX.

End of doc.
